---
title: "Spike2 (CED)"
---

[CED Spike2](https://ced.co.uk/products/spike2) records electrophysiology and behavioral signals into `.smr` or `.smrx` files. Neuralyzer loads Spike2 data through the optional [SonPy](https://pypi.org/project/sonpy/) Python package.

::: {.callout-warning}
## SonPy platform support

SonPy is advertised as cross-platform, but at the time of writing we have only been able to use it successfully on **Windows**. Attempts on Linux and macOS have failed; a bug report has been submitted to CED. Until that is resolved, plan on a Windows Python environment (local or remote) for Spike2 loading via the JSON `python` block below.
:::

Many labs record TTL-like signals on **ADC inputs** (continuous waveforms) rather than native Spike2 event/level channels. For those files, use `threshold` to derive `digital_event` or `digital_interval` series from the ADC trace. Use `data_type: "analog"` when you want the waveform itself (for example, a breathing sensor).

## Prerequisites

Neuralyzer ships `resources/python/whiskertoolbox_io/spike2_sonpy.py` next to the application binary (build tree and `cmake --install` layouts). You do not need `python_helper_path` in JSON unless you override the bundled helper.

Configure a Python environment that matches your Neuralyzer build (same major/minor Python version) and has SonPy installed:

```json
{
  "python": {
    "venv_path": "/path/to/sonpy-env",
    "required_imports": ["sonpy", "numpy"],
    "fail_on_missing_imports": true
  }
}
```

Place this `python` block at the top of your JSON config, before the `data` array.

## One entry per channel and output

Use **one `data[]` entry per SonPy channel and per output type**. Multiple entries may reference the same `.smrx` file. SonPy reads each channel independently.

Every Spike2 entry requires:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `format` | `"spike2"` |
| `filepath` | Path to `.smr` or `.smrx` (relative to the JSON file) |
| `channel` | SonPy channel index (integer) |
| `name` | Name registered in the DataManager |
| `data_type` | `"analog"`, `"digital_event"`, or `"digital_interval"` |

Optional fields:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `processing.invert` | Multiply samples by −1 before output or thresholding |
| `processing.subtract_mean` | Subtract the channel mean before output or thresholding |
| `threshold` | Values above this level form digital intervals; event times are interval starts |
| `clock` | [TimeFrame](../../concepts/timeframe.qmd) to assign (see below) |

When `threshold` is omitted, `digital_event` and `digital_interval` entries read **native** Spike2 event/level channels instead of thresholding an ADC waveform.

## Loading analog time series from an ADC channel

Load a breathing sensor or other continuous ADC trace as an `AnalogTimeSeries`:

```json
{
  "name": "breath",
  "format": "spike2",
  "data_type": "analog",
  "filepath": "recording.smrx",
  "channel": 3,
  "processing": { "invert": true, "subtract_mean": true },
  "clock": "master"
}
```

Omit `processing` when you want the raw ADC values.

## Loading digital events from an ADC channel

Threshold an ADC waveform to get rising-edge event times (for example, camera frame triggers):

```json
{
  "name": "camera_frames",
  "format": "spike2",
  "data_type": "digital_event",
  "filepath": "recording.smrx",
  "channel": 0,
  "processing": { "invert": true, "subtract_mean": true },
  "threshold": 2.0,
  "clock": "master"
}
```

## Loading digital intervals from ADC channels

Use the same `channel`, `processing`, and `threshold` settings as for events, but set `data_type` to `"digital_interval"`. Add one entry per channel:

```json
{
  "name": "sound_intervals",
  "format": "spike2",
  "data_type": "digital_interval",
  "filepath": "recording.smrx",
  "channel": 1,
  "threshold": 1.0,
  "clock": "master"
},
{
  "name": "laser_intervals",
  "format": "spike2",
  "data_type": "digital_interval",
  "filepath": "recording.smrx",
  "channel": 2,
  "threshold": 4.0,
  "clock": "master"
}
```

To also get **event** series (start times only) from the same ADC channels, add separate `digital_event` entries with the same `channel`, `processing`, and `threshold`.

## Assigning clocks

Spike2 data is stored in the file's native tick timebase. Neuralyzer [TimeFrames](../../concepts/timeframe.qmd) let you define how data aligns with video, derived event clocks, and other signals.

### Forward-declare clocks

List clock names at the top of the JSON so data can reference them before they are populated:

```json
{
  "clocks": ["master", "time"],
  "data": [ ... ]
}
```

### Master clock from an analog series

Span `master` from sample 0 through the last index of a loaded analog series:

```json
{
  "format": "max_value",
  "data_type": "time",
  "name": "master",
  "source_data": "breath"
}
```

Register analog Spike2 data on `master` with `"clock": "master"` so its samples share that timebase.

### Derived clock from digital events

Build a secondary `time` TimeFrame by sampling `master` at each event in a digital event series (for example, camera frames):

```json
{
  "format": "derived",
  "data_type": "time",
  "name": "time",
  "source_timeframe": "master",
  "source_series": "camera_frames",
  "source_type": "event"
}
```

Assign video or other data acquired on the camera clock with `"clock": "time"`.

### Deferred clock binding

Data entries may list `"clock": "master"` or `"clock": "time"` even when those TimeFrames are defined later in the `data` array. If the clock appears in `clocks`, data is registered on it immediately; otherwise binding is deferred until the end of loading.

## Complete example

Session with breath (ADC), camera frames (thresholded ADC events), two interval channels, master/derived clocks, and video on the derived clock:

```json
{
  "python": {
    "venv_path": "/path/to/sonpy-env",
    "required_imports": ["sonpy", "numpy"],
    "fail_on_missing_imports": true
  },
  "clocks": ["master", "time"],
  "data": [
    {
      "name": "breath",
      "format": "spike2",
      "data_type": "analog",
      "filepath": "recording.smrx",
      "channel": 3,
      "clock": "master"
    },
    {
      "name": "camera_frames",
      "format": "spike2",
      "data_type": "digital_event",
      "filepath": "recording.smrx",
      "channel": 0,
      "processing": { "invert": true, "subtract_mean": true },
      "threshold": 2.0,
      "clock": "master"
    },
    {
      "name": "sound_intervals",
      "format": "spike2",
      "data_type": "digital_interval",
      "filepath": "recording.smrx",
      "channel": 1,
      "threshold": 1.0,
      "clock": "master"
    },
    {
      "name": "laser_intervals",
      "format": "spike2",
      "data_type": "digital_interval",
      "filepath": "recording.smrx",
      "channel": 2,
      "threshold": 4.0,
      "clock": "master"
    },
    {
      "format": "max_value",
      "data_type": "time",
      "name": "master",
      "source_data": "breath"
    },
    {
      "format": "derived",
      "data_type": "time",
      "name": "time",
      "source_timeframe": "master",
      "source_series": "camera_frames",
      "source_type": "event"
    },
    {
      "name": "media",
      "data_type": "video",
      "filepath": "behavior.mp4",
      "clock": "time"
    }
  ]
}
```
